title: Parabolas, ellipses and hyperbolas
description: Questions on moving graphs, parabolas and their focus, ellipses, hyperbolas, cones and the general equation.

questions.question: To turn a graph by $$\varphi$$ about $$O$$, what do you put into its equation?
questions.explanation: A point is on the turned graph exactly when turning it back by $$\varphi$$ lands on the old graph (:ref{#turn-graph}). The same backwards rule is why $$x - 3$$ slides right.

questions.question: What does the half turn about $$O$$ do to the parabola $$y = x^2$$?
questions.explanation: For $$\varphi = \pi$$ the turned-back point is $$(-x, -y)$$ (:ref{#turn-graph}), so $$-y = (-x)^2 = x^2$$, which is $$y = -x^2$$: the cup upside down.

questions.question: Where is the centre of the circle $$(x - 2)^2 + y^2 = 1$$ after a quarter turn anticlockwise about $$O$$?
questions.explanation: For $$\varphi = \frac{\pi}{2}$$ put $$y$$ for $$x$$ and $$-x$$ for $$y$$ (:ref{#turn-graph}): $$(y - 2)^2 + x^2 = 1$$, the circle with centre $$(0, 2)$$. The turn sends the old centre $$(2, 0)$$ there.

questions.question: What is the vertex of $$y = 2x^2 - 12x + 13$$?
questions.explanation: $$2x^2 - 12x + 13 = 2(x - 3)^2 - 5$$, so the graph is $$y = 2x^2$$ slid by $$(3, -5)$$ (:ref{#quadratic-parabola}).

questions.question: How do the graphs of $$y = x^2$$ and $$y = 4x^2$$ compare?
options: They have different shapes, one is narrower
They have the same shape: a zoom takes one onto the other
questions.explanation: The zoom by $$\frac14$$ about $$O$$ sends $$y = x^2$$ onto $$y = 4x^2$$ (:ref{#parabola-zoom}). In the same way every parabola has the shape of $$y = x^2$$.

questions.question: How many points does a vertical line have in common with $$y = x^2$$?
options: Exactly one, so it is a tangent
Exactly one, but it is not a tangent
questions.explanation: Each $$x$$ gives one $$y$$, so a vertical line meets the parabola once (:ref{#line-parabola}). It is parallel to the axis and crosses into the inside, so it is not counted as a tangent (:ref{#parabola-tangent-def}).

questions.question: What is the tangent to $$y = x^2$$ at $$(2, 4)$$?
questions.explanation: The tangent at $$(p, p^2)$$ is $$y = 2px - p^2$$ (:ref{#parabola-tangent}). Check: $$x^2 - 4x + 4 = (x - 2)^2$$ has one root.

questions.question: Why is the graph of $$y = ax^2 + bx + c$$ symmetric about a vertical line?
options: It is $$y = ax^2$$ slid into place, and $$y = ax^2$$ is symmetric about the $$y$$-axis
It is taken from the picture
questions.explanation: Completing the square shows it is a slide of $$y = ax^2$$ (:ref{#quadratic-parabola}), which is unchanged by $$x \mapsto -x$$. This proves what Quadratics took from the picture (:ref{#parabolas-remark-proved}).

questions.question: Which points make up the curve with focus $$F$$ and directrix $$L$$?
options: The points twice as far from $$F$$ as from $$L$$
The points equally far from $$F$$ and from $$L$$
questions.explanation: That is the definition (:ref{#focus-directrix}). It gives a parabola (:ref{#parabola-focus-exists}).

questions.question: Where is the focus of $$y = x^2$$?
questions.explanation: $$y = ax^2$$ has focus $$(0, \frac{1}{4a})$$ (:ref{#parabola-focus-exists}). With $$a = 1$$ that is $$(0, \frac14)$$, and the directrix is $$y = -\frac14$$.

questions.question: On $$y = \frac{x^2}{4}$$, with focus $$(0, 1)$$ and directrix $$y = -1$$, how far is the point $$(2, 1)$$ from each?
questions.explanation: $$(2, 1)$$ is $$2$$ across from $$(0, 1)$$, and $$1 - (-1) = 2$$ above the directrix (:ref{#focus-parabola}).

questions.question: Why do satellite dishes have a parabola as their cross-section?
options: Signals arriving parallel to the axis all reflect through the focus
It is the shape a dish sags into
questions.explanation: The reflecting property (:ref{#parabola-reflection}) sends every incoming ray parallel to the axis to the focus, where the receiver sits.

questions.question: In the proof of the reflecting property, what is the tangent at $$P$$?
options: The perpendicular bisector of the focus $$F$$ and the foot $$N$$ on the directrix
questions.explanation: $$PF = PN$$, and the tangent is the perpendicular bisector of $$FN$$ (:ref{#focus-and-directrix-tangent}). The flip in it swaps $$N$$ and $$F$$, so the straight-on ray towards $$N$$ reflects towards $$F$$.

questions.question: How far across and how far up does $$\frac{x^2}{25} + \frac{y^2}{9} = 1$$ reach from its centre?
questions.explanation: At $$y = 0$$, $$x^2 = 25$$; at $$x = 0$$, $$y^2 = 9$$. It is the unit circle stretched by $$5$$ across and $$3$$ up (:ref{#ellipse-equation}).

questions.question: Where are the foci of $$\frac{x^2}{25} + \frac{y^2}{9} = 1$$?
questions.explanation: $$c = \sqrt{a^2 - b^2} = \sqrt{25 - 9} = 4$$ (:ref{#ellipse-foci}), on the long axis.

questions.question: For $$\frac{x^2}{25} + \frac{y^2}{9} = 1$$, what is the total distance from any of its points to the two foci?
questions.explanation: The total is $$2a = 10$$ for every point (:ref{#ellipse-foci}). For example $$(0, 3)$$ is $$5$$ from each focus.

questions.question: What is the eccentricity of $$\frac{x^2}{25} + \frac{y^2}{16} = 1$$?
questions.explanation: $$c = \sqrt{25 - 16} = 3$$ and $$e = \frac{c}{a} = \frac35$$ (:ref{#ellipse-eccentricity}).

questions.question: Which ellipses have eccentricity $$0$$?
questions.explanation: $$e = 0$$ exactly when $$c = 0$$, that is $$a = b$$ (:ref{#ellipse-eccentricity}).

questions.question: What is the area inside $$\frac{x^2}{25} + \frac{y^2}{9} = 1$$?
questions.explanation: Its inside is the unit disc stretched by $$5$$ and $$3$$ (:ref{#ellipse-equation}), so its area is $$\pi \cdot 5 \cdot 3$$ (:ref{#area-and-scaling/ellipse-area}).

questions.question: How many pieces does the graph of $$xy = 12$$ have?
options: Two branches, one top right and one bottom left
It is a pair of lines
questions.explanation: $$x$$ and $$y$$ must have the same sign, and neither can be $$0$$, so the curve has two separate branches. Turned by $$\frac{\pi}{4}$$ it becomes a standard hyperbola (:ref{#hyperbola-turn}), and every hyperbola has two branches.

questions.question: Turning the graph of $$xy = 2$$ by $$\frac{\pi}{4}$$ about $$O$$ gives which graph?
questions.explanation: The turn by $$\frac{\pi}{4}$$ sends $$xy = c$$ to $$y^2 - x^2 = 2c$$ (:ref{#hyperbola-turn}).

questions.question: What are the asymptotes of $$\frac{x^2}{9} - \frac{y^2}{16} = 1$$?
questions.explanation: The asymptotes are $$y = \pm\frac{b}{a}x$$ with $$a = 3$$ and $$b = 4$$ (:ref{#hyperbola-asymptotes}).

questions.question: Where are the foci of $$\frac{x^2}{9} - \frac{y^2}{16} = 1$$?
questions.explanation: For a hyperbola $$c = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2} = \sqrt{9 + 16} = 5$$ (:ref{#hyperbola-foci}). An ellipse would use $$a^2 - b^2$$ instead.

questions.question: For any point of $$\frac{x^2}{9} - \frac{y^2}{16} = 1$$, what is the difference of its distances to the two foci?
questions.explanation: The difference is $$2a = 6$$ for every point (:ref{#hyperbola-foci}). This is how navigation by timing radio signals locates a ship on a hyperbola.

questions.question: What is the centre of the graph of $$xy - 2x + 4y - 5 = 0$$?
questions.explanation: It is $$(x + 4)(y - 2) = -3$$ (:ref{#hyperbolas-moved-product}), the graph of $$xy = -3$$ slid by $$(-4, 2)$$.

questions.question: Tilting a torch further and further from the wall, which order of curves does the edge of its light trace?
questions.explanation: The plane $$z = mx + 1$$ cuts the cone in a circle at $$m = 0$$, an ellipse for $$m < 1$$, a parabola at $$m = 1$$ and a hyperbola for $$m > 1$$ (:ref{#cone-slices}).

questions.question: What is special about a plane that cuts the cone in a parabola?
options: It is parallel to a line of the cone, tilted exactly as steeply as its side
questions.explanation: The cone's sides have slope $$1$$, and the slice is a parabola exactly when $$m = 1$$ (:ref{#cone-slices}).

questions.question: The points whose distance to $$F$$ is $$e$$ times their distance to a line $$L$$ form a hyperbola when
questions.explanation: $$e < 1$$ gives an ellipse, $$e = 1$$ a parabola and $$e > 1$$ a hyperbola (:ref{#focus-directrix-e}).

questions.question: A comet's path has eccentricity about $$0.97$$. What does that say?
options: It passes once and never returns
It moves in a straight line
It is a long ellipse, so the comet keeps coming back
questions.explanation: Eccentricity less than $$1$$ means an ellipse (:ref{#ellipse-eccentricity}), a closed path. Halley's comet has $$e \approx 0.967$$ and returns about every $$75$$ years.

questions.question: What can a plane through the tip of the cone cut out?
options: A single point, one line or two crossing lines
questions.explanation: These are some of the degenerate cases (:ref{#degenerate-conic}), the slices through the tip.

questions.topic: Recognising a curve from its equation
questions.question: For $$Ax^2 + Bxy + Cy^2 + \dots = 0$$, which number tells the family of the curve?
questions.explanation: $$B^2 - 4AC$$ is unchanged when the axes are turned, and its sign names the family (:ref{#conic-discriminant}).

questions.topic: Recognising a curve from its equation
questions.question: What does $$x^2 + xy + y^2 = 3$$ draw?
questions.explanation: $$B^2 - 4AC = 1 - 4 = -3 < 0$$, so an ellipse, a point or nothing (:ref{#conic-discriminant}); the point $$(1, 1)$$ fits, and it is an ellipse.

questions.topic: Recognising a curve from its equation
questions.question: What is $$B^2 - 4AC$$ for $$xy = 1$$, and what does it say?
questions.explanation: Here $$A = C = 0$$ and $$B = 1$$, so $$B^2 - 4AC = 1 > 0$$ (:ref{#conic-discriminant}), as :ref{#hyperbola-turn} showed.

questions.topic: Recognising a curve from its equation
questions.question: For $$5x^2 - 6xy + 5y^2 = 8$$, by what angle do you turn to remove the $$xy$$ term?
questions.explanation: When $$A = C$$, the turn by $$\frac{\pi}{4}$$ works (:ref{#remove-xy}). It gives $$\frac{u^2}{4} + v^2 = 1$$, an ellipse.

questions.topic: Recognising a curve from its equation
questions.question: What is the graph of $$x^2 - y^2 = 0$$?
questions.explanation: $$x^2 - y^2 = (x - y)(x + y)$$ is $$0$$ exactly when one factor is $$0$$. It is a degenerate case (:ref{#degenerate-conic}).

questions.topic: Recognising a curve from its equation
questions.question: What is the graph of $$x^2 + y^2 = -1$$?
questions.explanation: A sum of squares is never negative, so no point fits. The discriminant says ellipse family, and this is its empty case (:ref{#no-xy-term}).
